facts.fact: Echos Sante reports that the Pandemic Fund's FCFA 13.44bn grant, within a FCFA 91.5bn (about US$160m) 2026-2029 project, has as a stated deliverable increased interoperability of Cameroon's national health information systems, with project activities launched on 2026-07-29.
facts.system: Pandemic Fund Cameroon pandemic prevention, preparedness and response project (national health information systems interoperability)

systems.system: Pandemic Fund Cameroon pandemic prevention, preparedness and response project (national health information systems interoperability)

note: Payroll story; no health systems exchange stated.
Opinion piece names the Kenya PPP only as an example; states nothing this study asks of the country.

facts.fact: The health ministry communique says the national interoperability platform, with OpenHIM and OpenFn on a server at CAMTEL, already hosts use cases in universal health coverage, interconnecting enrolment and billing systems, and that not all systems are yet connected.

note: US PEPFAR/donor funding for interoperable health information systems stated only as an aim; no exchange contracted, piloted or in service for the country.
Architecture and plans only; the DHIS2-BUNEC link is to the civil register, not between two health systems, and the patient index is yet to be chosen.

facts.fact: Cameroon's INS director general said an interoperability initiative between the civil registration system, the health information system and the INS central system is already being tested.
facts.system: Cameroon civil registration, health information and INS interoperability initiative
